title: A sky photo is expected to appear in Memories
preconditions: A adds a photo in Us.
B expects every shared photo to appear in Memories.
Neither has read the explanation of the two destinations.

actions.note: A chooses a photo for the sky.
B searches Memories for the same photo.

expected_behavior: The app makes clear that a sky photo and a dated memory are separate actions.
A sky photo does not silently become a dated memory.
The archive remains the complete place to browse dated content.
candidate_failure_modes: B concludes the photo failed to save.
A believes one action published to both destinations.
The app adds a second, unrequested copy to resolve the ambiguity.

observed_code_behavior: Us and Memories are intentionally separate destinations; sky photos are not dated memories.
Free and Plus see the same relationship home.
documented_requirement: The app makes clear that a sky photo and a dated memory are separate actions.

hypothetical_user_behavior: A fictional participant (Grace Tan) said: "We are auditing Aoi for things that do not need to exist. Walk through Us and Memories as you actually used them: the photo sky, the history control, the help panel, the add-photo action, the dated-memory action, the distinction between the two surfaces, and every label or decoration around them. For each one, ask out loud: "Why does this even exist?" Then say what would break if it were removed, and what it cost you. Name the three most useless things and the one thing you would keep. Do not propose a redesign; remove."

A fictional participant (Grace Tan) said: "Three to remove, out loud, as asked:

1. The photo sky. It is decorative. It has never been the archive. With VoiceOver it is just something extra that gets announced between me and my photos, and it costs me swipes I don't have.
2. The add-photo action. I have never used it. It is an unlabelled shape, so I abandoned it on the first pass and never went back.
3. The help panel. If I need help to find a memory, the screen has already failed me. I would rather the button were big and said what it does.

The one I would keep: the dated-memory action. I find photos by month, and that is the only control that tells me where in time I am standing. Remove it and I am back to scrolling a canvas and guessing.

What it cost me: every decoration is another swipe between me and the one thing I came for. Do not shrink the labels to make room for the sky."
Grace Tan assumes: the sky is decorative and not the archive
Grace Tan assumes: photos can be found by date
Hiro Tan assumes: a pending upload is safely queued
Hiro Tan assumes: deleting a local copy does not delete the shared copy
